opportunities.title: Propose vulnerability identity key and lifecycle schema
opportunities.summary: ### Summary Inspect the committed Anchore JSON fixtures and propose a schema for tracking vulnerabilities over time. Specifically: what combination of fields uniquely identifies "the same vulnerability" across scans? Candidates to evaluate include CVE ID alone, CVE + package name, CVE + package name + version, and CVE + package + image. Write up the tradeoffs, pick a recommendation, and sketch the analytics DB table(s) needed to support first_seen / last_seen / fixed_at / ignored_at / cleared_at fields. **Tech notes:** The Anchore JSON schema is documented at the Anchore project site; worth skimming before diving into fixtures. The goal of this spike is a decision, not code — resist the urge to start implementing. ### Acceptance criteria - [ ] Written proposal (markdown doc in PR) covering identity key options, tradeoffs, and a recommendation - [ ] Proposed analytics DB schema with column types and rationale - [ ] At least one worked example from the fixtures showing how the identity key behaves across days - [ ] Reviewed and approved by Brandon and/or Matt before next ticket starts ## Bounty: $250 This issue has been selected for our paid contributor program. opportunities.title: [bounty $400] Implement ABNF-compliant email address parser with full §3.2–§4.4 coverage
opportunities.summary: `source.md` contains the complete RFC 5322 specification (Internet Message Format). We need a **fully conformant email address parser** in Python that implements the complete ABNF grammar from sections 3.2 through 3.4, plus obsolete syntax from §4.4. opportunities.title: reward-manager: refund_pool moves funds with no require_auth at all
opportunities.summary: `contracts/reward-manager/src/lib.rs:558`: ```rust pub fn refund_pool(env: Env, creator: Address, hunt_id: u64) -> Result<(), RewardErrorCode> { let pool_config = Storage::get_pool_config(&env, hunt_id).ok_or(PoolNotFound)?; if creator != pool_config.creator { return Err(Unauthorized); } let balance = Storage::get_pool_balance(&env, hunt_id); if balance == 0 { return Ok(()); } ... client.transfer(&contract_addr, &creator, &balance); Storage::set_pool_balance(&env, hunt_id, 0); ``` There is **no `require_auth()`** — not even a `cfg`-gated one, unlike the five sites listed in the companion issue. The only check is an equality comparison against a caller-supplied address, which any caller satisfies by passing the creator's public address. The funds go to the legitimate creator, so this is not direct theft. It is worse in a specific way: **anyone can empty any hunt's reward pool at any moment**, including mid-hunt. Players who have already completed the hunt then hit `InsufficientPool` on `complete_hunt` and their earned rewards are unpayable. The attacker needs no relationship to the hunt and gains nothing — it is pure griefing, and it is free. **Fix** 1. Add `creator.require_auth();`

opportunities.summary: ## Context Next.js adds an `X-Powered-By: Next.js` header to every response by default. `next.config.ts` only sets `typedRoutes: true` and does not disable it. The header is an information leak that helps attackers fingerprint the framework (security issue #109 covers header policies but not this specific header). ## Proposed Change Set `poweredByHeader: false` in `next.config.ts`. Add a test using `next start` (or a production build check) asserting the header is absent from responses.

opportunities.title: nft-reward: initialize emits no event, so indexers cannot detect contract setup
opportunities.summary: `contracts/nft-reward/src/lib.rs:174-189` writes four pieces of state — admin, minter, max supply, contract version — and emits nothing. The contract emits events for far less consequential changes: `NftMinted`, `NftTransferred`, `NftMetadataUpdated`, `OperatorChanged`, `AdminImageUrisUpdated`. Initialization, which establishes who controls the contract and what the supply ceiling is, is silent. `add_authorized_contract:456`, `remove_authorized_contract:470`, and `set_reward_manager:443` are also silent — the entire authorization surface changes without any on-chain record. That makes it impossible for a monitor to alert on "the admin just authorized a new minter", which is precisely the event worth alerting on. `hunty-core` has the same gap for `initialize_admin:42` but does emit `RewardManagerSet` (`:857`). **Fix** Emit an initialization event carrying admin, minter, and max supply, and an event for every change to the admin or authorized-contract set. The `hunty-common` audit module (`contracts/common/src/audit_emitter.rs`) already provides `emit_audit_event` with the right shape — `ACTION_ADMIN_ADDED` and friends are defined and this is what they are for. **Acceptance criteria*

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
